sent_bad: You may pay up front for editing, design, or printing, though free e-publishing options exist and print-on-demand (IngramSpark) avoids paying to print and warehouse unsold copies.
**Why you want a writing career** — if money isn't a goal, knowing that up front saves you stress and rejection.

What it does show: traditional publishing can offer large advances (up to six figures or more) plus royalties and often higher sales, while self-publishing lets you start earning immediately but pays only what you sell, with possible up-front costs.
So the "greater profit" answer, per this document, is: it depends on your genre, audience, and whether you'd rather wait for a potential big advance or start selling now.
